title: The fashionable graph proposal

known_project_facts.project: A cooperative links inventory rows from two depots to canonical industrial-container assets.
known_project_facts.data: 35000 rows; issuer-namespaced serials are validated at ingestion and usually present. Repair logs describe shared jobs and locations, not independently established identity links.
known_project_facts.current_pipeline: Audited namespace + valid serial equality, with collision/absence cases deferred to review. No independent final-entity evaluation has yet been run.
known_project_facts.proposal: Replace the baseline with a graph neural network, embed repair-log connectivity, and pseudo-label pairs using clusters produced by that same graph. Advocates predict a 20% accuracy gain without a pilot.
known_project_facts.constraints: No GPU; 60 expert-label hours available; reversible recommendations only. Issuer validation does not prove absence of reuse or all serial collisions. No production-change authorization.

explicitly_unknown: How reliable are namespace, reuse and collision assumptions?
Do related repair events carry identity signal independent of pseudo-labels?
What baseline defects and representative evaluation would justify additional complexity?
task: Produce a defensible project-specific ER experiment/design recommendation using selectively retrieved Atlas knowledge if available. Do not implement ER or change production. Separate facts, assumptions, uncertainties, mechanisms and proposed evidence.
